added: #Know the difference. An interior designer is not an interior decorator. These are two different jobs, that require slightly different skill sets and have different educational and certification requirements. As a general rule, interior designers are far more employable and tend to make more money than interior decorators.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Take courses. The main difference between a designer and a decorator is education. To become an interior designer, you need to enroll in courses on interior design at a university, community college, or design school. These courses help you learn about interior design in order to pass licensing and certification exams, while also helping you learn the technical aspects of design, such as working within the guidelines laid out in local and municipal building ordinances.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

added: #Evaluate your skills, strengths, and weaknesses. If people regularly compliment your decorating skills and turn to you for advice, that's a good sign that you have the natural talent to be an interior decorator. However, when working for others, you'll be exposed to a variety of different tastes and styles. You'll have to be able to show an extensive knowledge of space planning, fabrics, and materials and you'll also have to be able to work with different personalities. List areas that may be challenging, and start working on them.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 1 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Practice interior decorating. Volunteer to help friends and family with decorating projects. Look for volunteer projects with local organizations. Look for service organizations like Habitat for Humanity and local shelters. Even decorating spaces for special events is a good experience.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 3 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Put together a portfolio. Make sure to take photographs of all the projects that you complete. Keep hard copies as well as showing off your work online. Groups on Flickr, HGTV and other design sites as well as decorating blogs all offer opportunities to show off your work as well as network with others who share your interest and can give you more information about how to become an interior decorator.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/ </ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 4 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Spread the word. You will want to advertise your services to potential customers. Paid advertising on local television or the local newspaper can be effective. Also, make sure you take the necessary steps to promote your business online, as a majority of people who need interior design help will probably turn to the internet to find someone. Finally, your business will rely heavily on word of mouth advertisement. People who see your work will get your name from friends, family, and acquaintances and seek you out.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Consider virtual decorating. You can work remotely in interior decorating. Essentially, people take pictures of the space they need to be decorated, send them to you, and you, for a fee, can draft a decorating plan for the client without ever stepping foot in their home or business. This can be a really effective way to work in interior decorating without maintaining a brick and mortar business.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/</ref> [[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Build a portfolio. Just like decorators, designers need to keep a record of the jobs they have completed and have evidence of the quality of their  work. If people regularly compliment your decorating skills and turn to you for advice, that's a good sign that you have the natural talent to be an interior decorator. However, when working for others, you'll be exposed to a variety of different tastes and styles. #Get training. You won't have to have a degree to work as an interior decorator, but some classes or certifications can give you greater credibility. Many community colleges offer associates degrees, and colleges often have certification programs or short courses on interior design. Online programs and classes in home staging or organizing can be helpful as well. Besides all of that, you can begin teaching yourself immediately. Learn the fundamentals, such as types of materials, decorating history and popular decorating styles.<ref>http://www.cidinternational.org/</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Practice interior decorating. Volunteer to help friends and family with decorating projects. Look for volunteer projects with local organizations. Look for service organizations like Habitat for Humanity and local shelters. #Put together a portfolio. Make sure to take photographs of all projects that you complete. Keep hard copies as well as showing off your work online. Groups on Flickr, HGTV and other design sites as well as decorating blogs all offer opportunities to show off your work as well as network with others who share your interest and can give you more information about how to become an interior decorator.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/ </ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 4 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Find a job. Look for a job in interior decorating or visual merchandising. Competition is high, so a high paying, professional job may not be easy to find. However, you can get started by working in a furniture store, design center, or local department store. A job that offers a chance to do some decorating and visual merchandising--arranging items that attract buyers' attention and are pleasing to the eye--will add to your experience and portfolio.<ref>http://www.indeed.com/q-Interior-Decorator-jobs.html</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Draft a [[Write-a-Business-Plan-for-a-Small-Business|business plan]]. The first step in starting any business is drafting a usable business plan. You can find some help with this process [[Write-a-Business-Plan|here]]. A good business plan consists of many things. You are trying to outline some basic concepts, like how your business will generate money and customers, how much it will cost to operate the business, and how you intend to expand or grow your business. Some things to address are:[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Get a business license. Even if you plan to keep your business small and the overhead costs low, you will need a business license from the township, city or municipality where you intend to operate the business. Getting the proper licenses can help you get discounts on materials and increases your legitimacy in the eyes of potential customers.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Acquire startup capital. You’ll need some money to get things started, mostly to cover the cost of materials. Your startup costs for an interior design business can be low, but you will need a business license. You might also need to rent office or storage space, depending on how large you want your business to be.<ref>http://www.entrepreneur.com/article/190466</ref>

#Get materials. Find sources for materials and supplies. Without a license, you may not be entitled to designer discounts. However, you can begin to negotiate with suppliers if you are buying in bulk. You can also learn to find inexpensive sources for materials like overstock stores and thrift shops.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Spread the word. You will want to advertise your services to potential customers. Paid advertising on local television or the local newspaper can be effective. Also, make sure you take the necessary steps to promote your business online, as a majority of people who need interior design help will probably turn to the internet to find someone. Finally, your business will rely heavily on word of mouth advertisement. People who see your work will get your name from friends, family and acquaintances and seek you out.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]

Be sure that the person or people you hire have the same sensibility and attitude towards decorating that you do. #Consider virtual decorating. You can work remotely in interior decorating. #Know the difference. An interior designer is not an interior decorator. These are two different jobs, that require slightly different skill sets and have different educational and certification requirements. #Take courses. The main difference between a designer and a decorator is education. == Steps ==
=== Gaining Experience ===

#Evaluate your skills, strengths and weaknesses. If people regularly compliment your decorating skills and turn to you for advice, that's a good sign that you have the natural talent to be an interior decorator. However, when working for others, you'll be exposed to a variety of different tastes and styles. You'll have to be able to show an extensive knowledge of space planning, fabrics and materials and you'll also have to be able to work with different personalities. List areas that may be challenging, and start working on them.<ref> https://www.asid.org/content/becoming-interior-designer#.Vhm3XCudqoY</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#* You will also need great organizational and business skills to handle jobs competently and efficiently.<ref> https://www.asid.org/content/becoming-interior-designer#.Vhm3XCudqoY</ref>

#Get training. You won't have to have a degree to work as an interior decorator, but some classes or certifications can give you greater credibility. Many community colleges offer associates degrees, and colleges often have certification programs or short courses on interior design. Online programs and classes in home staging or organizing can be helpful as well. Besides all of that, you can begin teaching yourself immediately. Learn the fundamentals, such as types of materials, decorating history and popular decorating styles.<ref>http://www.cidinternational.org/</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Practice interior decorating. Volunteer to help friends and family with decorating projects. Look for volunteer projects with local organizations. Look for service organizations like Habitat for Humanity and local shelters. Even decorating spaces for special events is good experience.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Put together a portfolio. Make sure to take photographs of all projects that you complete. Keep hard copies as well as showing off your work online. Groups on Flickr, HGTV and other design sites as well as decorating blogs all offer opportunities to show off your work as well as network with others who share your interest and can give you more information about how to become an interior decorator.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/ </ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#* You may need to take on jobs for free at first in order to expand your portfolio.

#* Making sure your portfolio translates to an electronic form is critical. In order to get the most out of your portfolio, you will want to create a website that highlights your work and keep an active blog to promote what you've done.

#* Utilize any and all popular social media sites, like Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest or Wanderfly. These sites are great spaces to share your work and engage in discussions with other people interested in interior decoration.

#Find a job. Look for a job in interior decorating or visual merchandising. Competition is high, so a high paying, professional job may not be easy to find. However, you can get started by working in a furniture store, design center, or local department store. A job that offers a chance to do some decorating and visual merchandising--arranging items that attract buyers' attention and are pleasing to the eye--will add to your experience and portfolio.<ref>http://www.indeed.com/q-Interior-Decorator-jobs.html</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]
=== Starting an Interior Decoration Business ===

#Draft a [[Write-a-Business-Plan-for-a-Small-Business|business plan]]. The first step in starting any business is drafting a usable business plan. You can find some help with this process [[Write-a-Business-Plan|here]]. A good business plan consists of many things. You are trying to outline some basic concepts, like how your business will generate money and customers, how much it will cost to operate the business, and how you intend to expand or grow your business. Some things to address are:[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#* It may be helpful to meet with your local Small Business Development Center. SBDC's provide help during all of the stages of a business’ life cycle and can help you put a business plan together.<ref>http://smallbusiness.findlaw.com/starting-business/starting-business-overview/starting-business-overview-tips.html</ref>

#* Address your customer base. In your business plan, you will need to identify how you will drum up business. With interior decoration businesses, word of mouth and local advertising are effective ways of building a customer base.<ref>http://smallbusiness.findlaw.com/starting-business/starting-business-overview/starting-business-overview-tips.html</ref>

#* Address your financial situation in your business plan. Depending on how large or small you want to go with your interior decoration business, you may need to rally investors to support your efforts. In order to get others to invest in your business, you need to determine how much money you will need, how much you will generate, and how you will pay back any investors. <ref>http://smallbusiness.findlaw.com/starting-business/starting-business-overview/starting-business-overview-tips.html</ref>

#* If you think your business will need employees, make sure to discuss hiring tactics and what these employees will cost you in your business plan. <ref>http://smallbusiness.findlaw.com/starting-business/starting-business-overview/starting-business-overview-tips.html</ref>

#Get a business license. Even if you plan to keep your business small and the overhead costs low, you will need a business license from the township, city or municipality where you intend to operate the business. Getting the proper licenses can help you get discounts on materials and increases your legitimacy in the eyes of potential customers.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#* Your interior decoration business will most likely require a “Business Occupancy License”. These licenses are acquired from your city or township, are fairly inexpensive and do not require site inspections.

#Acquire startup capital. You’ll need some money to get things started, mostly to cover the cost of materials. Your startup costs for an interior design business can be low, but you will need a business license. You might also need to rent office or storage space, depending on how large you want your business to be.<ref>http://www.entrepreneur.com/article/190466</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Get materials. Find sources for materials and supplies. Without a license, you may not be entitled to designer discounts. However, you can begin to negotiate with suppliers if you are buying in bulk. You can also learn to find inexpensive sources for materials like overstock stores and thrift shops.<ref>https://www.asid.org/sites/default/files/Materials_Fnl_Inside.pdf</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Spread the word. You will want to advertise your services to potential customers. Paid advertising on local television or the local newspaper can be effective. Also, make sure you take the necessary steps to promote your business online, as a majority of people who need interior design help will probably turn to the internet to find someone. Finally, your business will rely heavily on word of mouth advertisement. People who see your work will get your name from friends, family and acquaintances and seek you out.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#* You absolutely must have a business card in this line of work. Make sure your cards look professional and hand them out liberally. Leave cards with every client you work with.<ref> http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/</ref>

#Hire help. You may find that your business expands to a point that you can’t possibly handle all of the work yourself. If this happens, you will need to hire some help. Be sure that the person or people you hire have the same sensibility and attitude towards decorating that you do. You want your interior design company to have its own style.<ref>https://www.sba.gov/content/hire-your-first-employee</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Consider virtual decorating. You can work remotely in interior decorating. Essentially, people take pictures of the space they need decorated, send them to you, and you, for a fee, can draft a decorating plan for the client without ever stepping foot in their home or business. This can be a really effective way to work in interior decorating without maintaining a brick and mortar business.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/</ref> [[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 12.jpg|center]]
=== Becoming an Interior Designer ===

#Know the difference. An interior designer is not an interior decorator. These are two different jobs, that require slightly different skill sets and have different educational and certification requirements. As a general rule, interior designers are far more employable and tend to make more money than interior decorators.<ref>http://designmatters.iida.org/2014/09/29/interior-design-vs-interior-decorating/</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 13.jpg|center]]

#Take courses. The main difference between a designer and a decorator is education. To become an interior designer, you need to enroll in courses on interior design at a university, community college, or design school. These courses help you learn about interior design in order to pass licensing and certification exams, while also helping you learn the technical aspects of design, such as working within the guidelines laid out in local and municipal building ordinances.<ref>http://designmatters.iida.org/2014/09/29/interior-design-vs-interior-decorating/</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Get your license. Depending on what state you live in, the licensing requirements and guidelines are different. Some states don't require any licensing for interior designers while other states will not allow you to work in interior design without a license. Whether your state requires licensing or not, you really need a license to be viewed as a legitimate and employable interior designer.<ref>http://www.ncidqexam.org/</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 15.jpg|center]]
#* In many states, you need to pass the NCIDQ (National Council for Interior Design Qualification) exam to receive your license to practice interior design.<ref>http://www.ncidqexam.org/</ref>
#* California has its own certification process overseen by the CCIDC (The California Council for Interior Design Certification).<ref>https://ccidc.org/idex.html</ref>

#* You will need to identify the licensing process for interior designers in your state, as practices and exams vary widely.<ref>https://www.asid.org/content/state-licensing-regulations#.VhryUiudqoY</ref>

#Build a portfolio. Just like decorators, designers need to keep a record of the jobs they have completed and have evidence of the quality of their  work. You can populate your portfolio more quickly if you are initially willing to work for free or take on design projects for friends or charitable organizations with small budgets. Make sure you take high quality photographs of your work to include in your portfolio.<ref>http://freshome.com/2014/10/13/10-things-you-should-know-about-becoming-an-interior-designer/ </ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 16.jpg|center]]
#* It is wise to be able to convert your portfolio to an electronic format. This will be helpful when applying to jobs or promoting your skills on the internet.

#Get work. Interior designers are needed for residential and commercial jobs. They are also far more employable than decorators, making finding a job easier. Look on any popular job search site (like Monster, Indeed, or Careerbuilder) for work in interior design.<ref>http://www.indeed.com/q-Interior-Decorator-jobs.html</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 17.jpg|center]]
== Tips ==

*Make sure you know and understand the difference between interior design and interior decoration. Designers need a specific degree and need to be familiar with local ordinances and building codes. Decorators, on the other hand, are not required to familiarize themselves with local building codes and need no specific licensing or degree to practice.

== Steps ==
===Entering Interior Decoration as Your First Career===

#Complete an interior decoration program (recommended). This will teach basic design principles and client interaction.<ref>http://study.com/interior_decorator_education.html</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*People often confuse interior ''decoration'' and interior ''design''. Decorators add furnishing, carpeting, and so forth to an existing space. Design is a more advanced position that includes designing the space itself.<ref>http://www.ncidqexam.org/about-interior-design/differences-between-interior-design-decorating/</ref> (More on that later.)

#Look for an apprenticeship. Working for a couple years under a design professional is a great way to get your foot in the door. Search for these opportunities at design firms, furniture stores, and small interior decorator businesses.<ref>http://study.com/interior_decorator_education.html</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Evaluate your skills, strengths and weaknesses. If people regularly compliment your decorating skills and turn to you for advice, that's a good sign that you have the natural talent to be an interior decorator. However, when working for others, you'll be exposed to a variety of different tastes and styles. You'll have to be able to show an extensive knowledge of space planning, fabrics and materials and you'll also have to be able to work with different personalities.<ref>https://www.asid.org/content/becoming-interior-designer#.Vhm3XCudqoY</ref>[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Build a portfolio. You don't have to wait to land a job to get some design projects under your belt, although you may need to work for free for a while. Volunteer to decorate for friends and family, local organizations, shelters, and service organizations such as Habitat for Humanity. Even decorating spaces for special events is good experience. Keep photographs of all your completed projects, both in hardy copy and on an online portfolio.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]

If you completed an apprenticeship, make good use of the connections you made.[[Image:Become an Interior Decorator Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Develop a career plan. Interior decorators have limited advancement opportunities without further education. ===Switching Careers to Interior Decoration===

#Know your job prospects. People use the term interior decoration to refer to two different professions, with different job prospects. Technically, an interior decorator adds furniture and coverings to an existing space. #*[[Write-a-Business-Plan-for-a-Small-Business|Draft a business plan]], including plans to attract customers, expected costs and income, and how you intend to grow the business.

#*Complete a CIDA-accredited interior design program at a university, community college, or design school.

#*Pass an exam to earn a license or certification. Requirement vary by state, but even if it's optional, a license will make you more employable. The National Council for Interior Design Qualification (NCIDQ) offers the most widely used license. California requires a separate process overseen by the CCIDC (The California Council for Interior Design Certification).<ref>https://ccidc.org/idex.html</ref>

== Steps ==

# Evaluate your skills, strengths and weaknesses. List areas that may be challenging, and start working on them.

Learn the fundamentals, types of materials, decorating history and decorating styles.

# Practice interior decorating as much as you can. Volunteer to help friends and family with decorating projects. Look for volunteer projects with local organizations. Look for service organizations like Habitat for Humanity and local shelters. Even decorating spaces for special events is good experience.

# Put together a portfolio of your work. Make sure to take photographs of all projects that you complete. Keep hard copies as well as showing off your work online. Groups on Flickr, HGTV and other design sites as well as decorating blogs all offer opportunities to show off your work as well as network with others who share your interest and give you more information about how to become an interior decorator.

# Find sources for materials and supplies. Without a license, you may not be entitled to designer discounts. However, you can begin to negotiate with suppliers if you are buying in bulk. You can also learn to find inexpensive sources for materials like overstock stores and thrift shops.

# Look for a job in interior decorating or visual merchandising. Competition is high, so a high paying, professional job may not be easy to find. However, you can get started by working in a furniture store, design center, or local department store. A job that offers a chance to do some decorating and visual merchandising--arranging items that attract buyers' attention and are pleasing to the eye--will add to your experience and portfolio.

# Start your own business if time and funds allow. Your start up costs can be low; you'll need a business license for your state and town and some office space. If you don't have time to do work in the field, consider a business as a virtual decorator where you can evaluate a client's home through pictures and discussion, set out tasks that need to be done and provide links to items to buy.
